paper.title: Statler: State-Maintaining Language Models for Embodied Reasoning
paper.central_claim: Prompting LLMs as world-state reader and writer so an explicit state estimate is maintained and conditions each action significantly outperforms Code-as-Policies on robot planning tasks and may scale to long-horizon tasks.
paper.scope_decision: in_scope: prompted LLM reader/writer harness over Code-as-Policies primitives controlling a simulated and a real UR5 tabletop arm.

preliminary_judgment: Written after reading the fixed text, before opening this paper's seat records: system_method. 3 sim domains x 20 author-designed episodes with hard history queries, step success judged against gold code, CaP 0 episodes vs Statler 0.40-0.55; temporal-query split; 10 real UR5 episodes 40% vs 20%; ablations w/o state/Unified/Auto (Auto wins 2/3). LLM for experiments unnamed; prompts partly elided with repository pointer. Expected online (real counts), scoped, holdout 2, cost weak.

signatures.persistence: state stored in external memory within an episode

gap.author_gap: Model-free LLM planners must track world state implicitly; temporal/history-dependent queries and unobservable state fail, and the problem grows with horizon.
gap.checked_gap: Supported by the paper's own diagnostic: near-perfect non-temporal vs 0-31% temporal query accuracy for CaP (Table II). Nearest neighbours are CaP and CaP+CoT (run) and scratchpad/state-tracking work (cited, not fetched).

claims.text: Maintaining an explicit LLM-estimated world state significantly outperforms CaP and CaP+CoT on tabletop tasks needing reasoning over history.
claims.setting: PyBullet tabletop (pick-and-place, disinfection, relative weight), 20 episodes of 5-16 queries each
claims.baseline_control: CaP, CaP+CoT with equivalent demonstrations; Statler w/o State equals CaP
claims.selection_vs_test: prompts designed per domain; queries chosen to be challenging; overlap not stated
claims.result_denominator: Episode success 0.50/0.40/0.55 (steps 0.88/0.82/0.93) vs CaP 0/0/0; CaP+CoT 0.25/0.00/0.30; n=20 per cell
claims.allowed_conclusion: Large gain over CaP on authors' hard history-dependent episodes; CoT comparison confounded by context limit.

claims.result_denominator: Table II counts, e.g. CaP 9/29 vs Statler 48/58 on pick-and-place; denominators differ because only the prefix before first failure is scored
claims.allowed_conclusion: Directionally supported; accuracy not computed on matched query sets.

claims.setting: UR5, MDETR segmentation, stacking/cover tasks, 10 episodes
claims.selection_vs_test: tasks designed with prompt development by authors
claims.allowed_conclusion: Small n; direction consistent with simulation.

claims.text: Reader/writer split is better than unified.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Weak: authors themselves attribute part to prompt sensitivity and Auto wins on two domains.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Online on the strength of 10 counted real-robot episodes with success rates; simulated results are gold-code correctness. Not transfer: the real domain's tasks and prompts were developed with the method.
assessment.author_claim_preserved: Prompting LLMs as world-state reader and writer so an explicit state estimate is maintained and conditions each action significantly outperforms Code-as-Policies on robot planning tasks and may scale to long-horizon tasks.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 20 author-designed history-dependent episodes per simulated domain (scored against gold code) and 10 real UR5 episodes, an LLM-written world-state estimate consulted by a code-writing reader completes 40-55% (sim) / 40% (real) of episodes where Code-as-Policies completes 0% / 20%; the gain comes from maintaining state, not specifically from the reader/writer split.
assessment.cannot_be_claimed: Scaling to longer-horizon tasks (untested beyond 16 steps); superiority of the two-role design over a single or instruction-only writer; reliability of the written state; results for a named or different LLM.
assessment.retained: not_applicable: within-episode state, no cross-task retained improvement

measurement.reason: Both seats 2. Episode/step success with counts (20 per domain, 10 real) and an episode-failure rule, but simulated steps are scored against gold code (agg:E001) rather than simulator end state, Table II scores survivor prefixes with unmatched denominators, the hard queries were chosen by the authors, and real step denominators are not given.

causality.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 2). Same demonstrations across CaP, CaP+CoT, w/o State, Unified and Auto isolate the state-maintenance factor; Unified and Auto also beat CaP, so the gain is attributable to maintaining state rather than to the particular two-role prompt. Unseparated: extra writer call per step, CoT handicapped by context overflow in one domain, one unnamed LLM, and the reader/writer split itself (Auto wins 2/3) - which narrows the sub-claim, not the central one. Not 4.

holdout.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 1). Demonstrations and evaluation episodes come from the same author-built domains with no stated split and hand-picked hard queries (anchor 2 overlap). The real UR5 domain (cups covering objects, MDETR perception) is a different setup where the advantage persists (40% vs 20%), but its prompts were developed by the authors for it (agg:E004), so not 3.
